importantNotes: The walls were rebuilt in just 52 days — a remarkable achievement against opposition.
'The joy of the LORD is your strength' (8:10) — spoken when the people wept at hearing God's Law.
Nehemiah's arrow prayers throughout the book model bringing everything to God instantly.
Nehemiah was a cupbearer to the king — God uses people in every occupation.
The book shows that physical rebuilding and spiritual renewal must go hand in hand.

chapters.1: Nehemiah hears about Jerusalem's broken walls; he mourns, fasts, and prays.
chapters.2: Nehemiah requests and receives permission from King Artaxerxes to rebuild Jerusalem's walls.
chapters.3: The various gates and sections of the wall are assigned to different families and groups.
chapters.4: Sanballat and Tobiah mock and threaten; Nehemiah arms the workers and continues building.
chapters.5: Nehemiah addresses economic injustice — the wealthy are exploiting the poor.
chapters.6: Enemies plot against Nehemiah; the wall is completed in 52 days.
chapters.7: The list of returned exiles; Jerusalem's population is still small.
chapters.8: Ezra reads the Law publicly; the people weep and celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
chapters.9: A day of national confession and prayer; the Levites recount Israel's history.
chapters.10: The people make a binding covenant to follow God's law — tithes, Sabbath, and no intermarriage.
chapters.11: The repopulation of Jerusalem; leaders and families who settled in the city.
chapters.12: The dedication of the wall with great celebration, music, and thanksgiving.
chapters.13: Nehemiah's final reforms — he corrects Sabbath violations, tithing failures, and intermarriage.
